newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians protest over U.S. vote on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians protest over U.S. vote on Jerusalem.

text.p: Prominent Palestinians protested outside the U.S. consulate in Arab East Jerusalem on Monday against a House of Representatives resolution identifying the entire city as Israel's undivided capital.
"If this will be a decision adopted by the United States, it is the end of this peace process," Faisal al-Husseini, the top PLO official in Jerusalem, told reporters at the demonstration.
The non-binding resolution, passed by a 406-17 House vote on Thursday, also called on President Bill Clinton to move the U.S. embassy to Jerusalem.
The resolution angered Arabs at a time when Israeli-Palestinian relations are in crisis over the construction of a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.
The protesters said the House decision undermined Washington's credibility as a sponsor of the Middle East peace process.
"America is submitting itself now to Zionist pressures by taking this hostile stand," said Jerusalem's Mufti Ikrima Sabri, the highest Moslem religious authority in the West Bank and Gaza.
"We reject America as a co-sponsor of the so-called negotiations because America has unveiled its ugly face," he said.
Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it in a move that has not been recognized by the international community, including the United States.

Israel claims Jerusalem as its undivided capital. But Palestinians regard the eastern part of the city as the capital of what they say will be their own future state. They say the United States should not pre-empt final status peace talks by taking a position on Jerusalem.
